rule.description: One file-handle capability trait bundles four distinct I/O directions so implementors must discharge directions they cannot honor (unconditional refusal stubs) and consumers must demand the entire bundle while exercising only a subset.

checks.description: A single trait declaration bundling three or more distinct I/O capability directions for file handles, obligating every implementor and consumer to accept all bundled directions.
checks.detected_relation: capability trait declaration -> bundled direction obligation imposed on all implementors and consumers
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The interface exceeds every handle's dependency boundary by fusing unrelated capabilities (sequential read, sequential write, durability/truncation, position/length) that different handles and consumers need independently.

matches.evidence: The merged file capability declaration bundles four I/O directions (sequential read, sequential write, durability/truncation, position/length) into a single trait, obligating every implementor and consumer to accept all of them.

checks.description: An implementor of the bundled capability interface discharges a bundled direction it cannot honor with an unconditional runtime-rejection body instead of a real implementation.
checks.detected_relation: implementor type -> bundled capability method it is forced to reject outright
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The implementor never needed that capability; the refusal only exists to satisfy the fused interface, which is exactly the method-injection burden interface segregation forbids.

matches.evidence: Impl of the merged trait for Vec<u8>: method fread_exact returns Err(Unsupported) unconditionally ("in-memory buffer is write-only") because the single capability interface obligates a direction this handle cannot honor.

Impl of the merged trait for Vec<u8>: method f_cursor returns Err(Unsupported) unconditionally ("in-memory buffer has no cursor") because the single capability interface obligates a direction this handle cannot honor.

Impl of the merged trait for Vec<u8>: method f_seek_start returns Err(Unsupported) unconditionally ("in-memory buffer has no cursor") because the single capability interface obligates a direction this handle cannot honor.

Impl of the merged trait for BufferedReader: method fwrite returns Err(Unsupported) unconditionally ("buffered reader is read-only") because the single capability interface obligates a direction this handle cannot honor.

Impl of the merged trait for BufferedReader: method fsync_all returns Err(Unsupported) unconditionally ("buffered reader does not manage durability") because the single capability interface obligates a direction this handle cannot honor.

Impl of the merged trait for BufferedReader: method fsync_data returns Err(Unsupported) unconditionally ("buffered reader does not manage durability") because the single capability interface obligates a direction this handle cannot honor.

Impl of the merged trait for BufferedReader: method f_truncate returns Err(Unsupported) unconditionally ("buffered reader is read-only") because the single capability interface obligates a direction this handle cannot honor.

Impl of the merged trait for BufferedWriter: method fread_exact returns Err(Unsupported) unconditionally ("buffered writer is write-only") because the single capability interface obligates a direction this handle cannot honor.

Impl of the merged trait for BufferedWriter: method f_len returns Err(Unsupported) unconditionally ("buffered writer is write-only") because the single capability interface obligates a direction this handle cannot honor.

Impl of the merged trait for BufferedWriter: method f_cursor returns Err(Unsupported) unconditionally ("buffered writer is write-only") because the single capability interface obligates a direction this handle cannot honor.

Impl of the merged trait for BufferedWriter: method f_seek_start returns Err(Unsupported) unconditionally ("buffered writer is write-only") because the single capability interface obligates a direction this handle cannot honor.

checks.description: A generic consumer (method taking a `impl`-parameter or generic handle bounded by the bundled trait) demands every bundled I/O direction while its body exercises only a strict subset.
checks.detected_relation: generic consumer body -> bundled I/O directions demanded by its bound but never exercised
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The consumer's dependency footprint is the whole capability bundle, so callers must supply a full-capability handle for a task needing one direction; the consumer depends on capabilities it does not use.

The handle parameter of read_buffer requires the merged file capability trait (all four I/O directions), but the body only exercises read.
The handle parameter of read_full requires the merged file capability trait (all four I/O directions), but the body only exercises read, position/length.

The handle parameter of file_length requires the merged file capability trait (all four I/O directions), but the body only exercises position/length.

The handle parameter of write_buffer requires the merged file capability trait (all four I/O directions), but the body only exercises write.
The handle parameter of fsync_all requires the merged file capability trait (all four I/O directions), but the body only exercises durability/truncate.
The handle parameter of fsynced_write requires the merged file capability trait (all four I/O directions), but the body only exercises write, durability/truncate.
The handle parameter of truncate requires the merged file capability trait (all four I/O directions), but the body only exercises durability/truncate.
The handle parameter of read_buffer requires the merged file capability trait (all four I/O directions), but the body only exercises read.
The handle parameter of file_cursor requires the merged file capability trait (all four I/O directions), but the body only exercises position/length.
The handle parameter of file_length requires the merged file capability trait (all four I/O directions), but the body only exercises position/length.
The handle parameter of seek_from_start requires the merged file capability trait (all four I/O directions), but the body only exercises position/length.
The handle parameter of read_full requires the merged file capability trait (all four I/O directions), but the body only exercises read, position/length.
The handle parameter of fsynced_write requires the merged file capability trait (all four I/O directions), but the body only exercises write, durability/truncate.

excluded: The disk-backed file handle's merged impl block (interface/fs.rs, impl FileIo for File): it forwards every bundled direction faithfully to the backing std file; an honest full-capability implementor is not itself a rule match.

The local/virtual test-context bridge (interface/fs.rs, impl<Lf: FileIo> FileIo for AnyFile<Lf>): it forwards every demanded direction to a capable backing handle, so it neither rejects a direction nor over-demands one.

Import-list and doc-link rewrites in the file-format upgrade module, the v2 raw journal, and the journal recovery tests: carrying the merged name is a consequence of the bundle, not an independent match site.

Trait families outside the file-handle capability surface (journal adapters, event-log/batch-adapter specs, encoding-layer source/persist/map traits, index subsystem key/value/index-shape traits): bundling along their own capability axes is intentionally outside this rule's scope.
